what: S31: how fast can frames leave the N6 for the Pi over USB? With no SD card fitted this decides whether 30 fps HD is deliverable at all.
board: OpenMV N6 on nereus002, stock OpenMV v5.0.1 (rolled back)
host: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W, single DWC2 OTG port, unpowered Terminus hub, AE3 idle on the same hub

link.note: Both are the HIGH-SPEED values. The by-id descriptor says 'in FS Mode' but that string is cosmetic here -- it comes from pdev->dev_speed in usbd_desc.c:115 and does not track what the link negotiated. Confirmed independently by the S30 session on both rigs.

measurements.why: Measures mpremote's raw-REPL escaping, not the link. Off by ~2000x. Do not use.

measurements.method: pyserial direct off the CDC port
pyserial direct off the CDC port
pyserial direct off the CDC port

caveats: Link only. The board sends a precomputed constant buffer -- no capture, no encode, no disk write on the Pi. It answers 'can the wire carry it', not 'does the pipeline sustain it'.
AE3 was idle. Both boards share one Zero 2 W OTG port through one hub, so a two-camera pipeline contends for this same 19-20 MB/s.
The S30 session measured this N6 streaming HD q90 at 3.6 fps = ~1.5 MB/s. That is ~13x below the link and is therefore the stream IMPLEMENTATION, not USB.
